article_title: A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program
citation: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959
title: A two-year universal quantum technology master's curriculum balancing hardware and software skills (UQTEP)
description: The article proposes a novel two-year master's curriculum in quantum science and technology that aims at a balance between quantum hardware and software skills. It is structured into four semesters moving from core quantum foundations to specialization tracks and a final research project, thesis, or internship. The authors state the program is meant to "enhance the employability of professionals thereby reducing the skill shortage" faced by academic institutions and organizations.
requirements: A dedicated syllabus with enrichment of varied research areas to build a research mindset
Coverage of both hardware and software aspects of quantum technology
constraints: Proposed curriculum, not yet implemented or evaluated by the authors
target_learners: Master's-level students and professionals entering the quantum technology workforce
target_learning_goals: Deep conceptual understanding of quantum science and technology
examples: The paper lays out semester-by-semester subjects: core quantum mechanics and quantum information in year 1, hardware and software specialization in semester 3, and a research project, thesis, or internship in semester 4
key_sources: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959

article_title: A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program
citation: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959
title: Course framework built on problem-based learning, diversified learning opportunities, and interest-based specializations
description: The article describes the pedagogical framework of the proposed program as resting on three fundamental ideas: diversified learning opportunities supporting deep conceptual understanding, teaching most modules using problem-based learning, and offering specializations aligned with student interests because quantum computing is a diverse field with a wide range of applications. The framework positions the curriculum at the cutting edge of current quantum technology research trends.
requirements: Modules incorporating modern research issues such as quantum error correction and fault tolerance
Practical laboratory sessions and a sizable second-year research project
constraints: Designed for the rapidly dynamic nature of the quantum field, requiring continual updating of module content
target_learners: Master's students in quantum science and technology
target_learning_goals: Capacity for successful application of technical and professional skills
Conversance with the most recent advances in quantum science and technology
examples: Students are introduced to quantum error correction and fault tolerance in the quantum information and computing module; the quantum software development and simulation module contains instruction on quantum algorithms and quantum machine learning
key_sources: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959

citation: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959
title: UQTEP compulsory modules: quantum algorithms, semiconductor devices, laboratory and research skills, quantum photonics
description: The curriculum defines compulsory subjects binding together the hardware and software aspects of quantum technology. Introduction to Quantum Algorithms covers "quantum gates, qubits (quantum bits), and quantum circuits" including Shor's and Grover's algorithms; Semiconductor Devices covers diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs and IC fabrication; Laboratory and Research Skills offers practical lab instruction operating quantum systems; Introduction to Quantum Photonics covers photon generation, control and measurement.
requirements: Students should have foundations enabling them to analyze problems and identify appropriate quantum algorithms
Hands-on exercises and projects to reinforce theoretical notions
target_learners: Master's students specializing in quantum hardware or software pathways
target_learning_goals: Foundational grasp of quantum algorithms and their applications in cryptography, optimization, simulation, and machine learning
Bridging theoretical understanding and actual implementation of quantum principles
examples: The Laboratory and Research Skills course offers practical lab instruction where students operate, manipulate, and conduct experiments with quantum systems
key_sources: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959

article_title: A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program
citation: Sanjay Vishwakarma, Shalini D, Srinjoy Ganguly, Sai Nandan Morapakula. (2023). A Universal Quantum Technology Education Program. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15959
title: Interdisciplinary curriculum design crossing physics, computer science, engineering, and mathematics with collaborative projects
description: The article holds that quantum technology is intrinsically interdisciplinary and transcends conventional divisions between physics, computer science, engineering, and mathematics. The program therefore emphasizes interdisciplinary learning and cooperation through a core curriculum spanning multiple fields, elective courses outside the student's primary field, interdisciplinary group projects, and cross-disciplinary second-year research projects.
requirements: Elective courses unrelated to the primary field of study
Group projects involving interdisciplinary teams of students solving challenging issues
target_learners: Master's students from hardware, software, and superconducting circuits pathways
target_learning_goals: A wide understanding of quantum technology that crosses several traditional subjects
examples: A student specializing in the hardware pathway can take a module in quantum machine learning or quantum cryptography to gain software-side exposure
